set.body:
Scheduling lane: maintenance. Current plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md. Live dependency edges supersede historical sequencing below.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19; governing docs/refactor/PLAN.md.
Original six-type report predates sealing work; re-inventory every named type at the implementation SHA and probe from an external package before changing code. Retain unresolved holes only; do not repeat already-landed conversions. Mandatory for the surfaces exported as checked.

Original scope retained below for evidence; fleet procedure/assignments are historical and do not govern single-developer work.

FINDING: EVERY AlignWire INVARIANT IS ADVISORY OUTSIDE PACKAGE align, INCLUDING THE ONES I ADDED
TODAY. Demonstrated, not argued. Read-only; nothing edited, no candidate, and this touches files I
hold so I am reporting before deciding anything.

`CostBreakdown` is a case class with a `private[align]` constructor. In Scala 3 that still derives
Mirror.ProductOf, whose fromProduct rebuilds the type field by field without consulting AlignWire.
This is the SAME defect the team already fixed on PlacementResolution - which was made a plain final
class precisely to remove the Mirror - and on the RecallGraph slice.

FORGED FROM package storymodel4s.codec, outside align, in one call:
  total        = -7.0                    wire requires finite and >= 0
  supportWeight = 5.0                    wire requires [0, 1]
  Semantic     present AND missing       wire refuses the combination
  Granularity  imputed, NOT priced, and NOT in MayBeImputed   both of today's new guards
Every invariant violated simultaneously. The real door, handed the identical values, refuses:
  "CostBreakdown: supportWeight must be finite and in [0, 1]"

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL HERE: the package that can forge is the CODEC, which is exactly
where untrusted wire data enters. The v3 decode path does currently go through
AlignWire.costBreakdown - I checked - so nothing is broken today. But the guarantee I have been
writing into docstrings all day is not the guarantee that exists. hsmm/v3 says imputedTerms may name
only Semantic; that is true of the checked door and false of the type.

I WANT TO BE PRECISE ABOUT SEVERITY, because I got this wrong once already today: THIS PERMITS, IT
DOES NOT OCCUR. No code uses fromProduct on CostBreakdown; the codec goes through the factory. So
nothing is being corrupted. The argument for fixing it anyway is the argument the team already
accepted for PlacementResolution: an unforgeable constructor forecloses the possibility, and
"nobody does it today" is what makes a hole survive until someone does.

SIX TYPES SHARE THE SHAPE, all in cost.scala:
  StructuralMemberEstimate, StructuralMemberExclusion, StructuralReductionReceipt,
  StructuralReduction, CostBreakdown, Admissibility
I demonstrated CostBreakdown only. The others have validating factories in AlignWire too
(memberEstimate rejects non-finite, memberExclusion requires a contradiction), so I expect the same
result, but I have not run it and will not claim it.

NOT PROPOSING A CANDIDATE. The fix is the PlacementResolution treatment - plain final class with
hand-written equals/hashCode - and applied to six types it is a large mechanical change that would
collide with two candidates of mine already awaiting a merge gate (7adce14 touches CostBreakdown
directly). It should be its own bead, after those land, and probably its own review. Flagging it now
so it is on the record rather than rediscovered.

ONE THING I WOULD FLAG TO WHOEVER TAKES IT: the hand-written equals that comes with the fix is not
free. I made exactly that mistake on PlacementResolution this evening - added a field, forgot
equals, and two summaries differing only in why mass was excluded compared EQUAL until a test caught
it. Six types times every future field is a standing tax, and it is worth deciding deliberately
rather than pattern-matching on the earlier fix.

Incidental, from the same audit: wire.scala's private `clamp` has a NaN branch that cannot be
reached - memberEstimate rejects non-finite observed values, so the reduced value is always finite.
Unlike the imputed-and-missing check I removed, this one is defensible: it exists to mirror
DefaultLocalCostModel.clamp exactly so the receipt comparison is like-for-like, and its docstring
says so. Recording it so the next person auditing NaN branches does not have to re-derive that.
set.title: [maintenance] align: CostBreakdown and five sibling types are forgeable via Mirror.fromProduct, so every AlignWire invariant is advisory outside package align
